attributes.title: hayabusa-*

attributes.description: Programs seen fewest times. Malware is rare; legitimate software is common. Random-looking names here are worth immediate attention.

query.query: process.name: *

attributes.title: RAREST programs (least-frequency analysis)

attributes.description: One-off command lines. Attacker commands are usually unique; scheduled tasks and scripts repeat.

query.query: process.command_line: *

attributes.title: RAREST command lines

attributes.description: Rarest launch relationships. services.exe spawning calc.exe, or winword.exe spawning powershell.exe, are the shapes to look for.

query.query: process.parent.name: *

attributes.title: Unusual parent -> child process pairs

attributes.description: Accounts appearing least often. Newly created or attacker-used accounts surface here before anything alerts on them.

query.query: user.name: *

attributes.title: RAREST user accounts

attributes.description: Rules explicitly naming hacking tools or suspicious binaries.

query.query: rule.name: (*HackTool* or *Suspicious* or *Malicious* or *Mimikatz*)

attributes.title: HackTools and suspicious executables

attributes.description: Living-off-the-land binaries: signed Microsoft tools abused to download, execute or bypass controls.

query.query: process.name: ("certutil.exe" or "mshta.exe" or "regsvr32.exe" or "rundll32.exe" or "wscript.exe" or "cscript.exe" or "bitsadmin.exe" or "wmic.exe" or "msbuild.exe" or "installutil.exe" or "regasm.exe" or "odbcconf.exe" or "forfiles.exe" or "pcalua.exe" or "desktopimgdownldr.exe")

attributes.title: LOLBin usage

attributes.description: Which interpreters ran, split by severity.

query.query: process.name: ("powershell.exe" or "pwsh.exe" or "cmd.exe" or "python.exe" or "wscript.exe" or "cscript.exe" or "mshta.exe" or "bash.exe")

attributes.title: Script interpreters

attributes.description: base64, -enc, -bypass, hidden windows. Deliberate evasion, not normal admin work.

query.query: process.command_line: (*enc* or *EncodedCommand* or *FromBase64* or *bypass* or *hidden* or *noprofile* or *DownloadString* or *IEX*)

attributes.title: Encoded / obfuscated commands

attributes.description: Source IPs that are not RFC1918/loopback/multicast. Pivot these into Hunt against Zeek and Suricata.
attributes.title: Connections OUTSIDE the network

attributes.description: How an attacker survives a reboot. Service installs are the classic lateral-movement footprint.

query.query: rule.name: (*Service* or *Registry* or *Autorun* or *Scheduled* or *Startup* or *Persist* or *WMI*)

attributes.title: Persistence: services, autoruns, scheduled tasks

attributes.description: Attacker activity often clusters outside business hours. Bars far from the normal working-day shape deserve a look.

query.query: event.severity >= 50

attributes.description: Each executable with its SHA-256 and the number of hosts it ran on. A program on ONE host, or one name with several hashes, is the lead. Hashes exist only where Sysmon was installed; copy one into VirusTotal or your TI platform.

query.query: file.hash.sha256: *

attributes.title: 6. Programs with hashes - on how many hosts

attributes.description: Event 7045/4697: a service was installed. PsExec, remote admin tools and much ransomware arrive this way. Binaries in Temp, ProgramData, Users or with random names are the ones to open.

query.query: event.code: ("7045" or "4697")

attributes.title: 7. Services installed - host > service > binary

attributes.description: Autoruns and other persistence keys (Sysmon 12-14) seen least often.

query.query: registry.path: *

attributes.title: 8. RAREST registry keys written

attributes.description: Files written (Sysmon 11/23) and file paths named by other rules, rarest first. Scripts and executables dropped in user-writable folders stand out.

query.query: file.path: * and not event.code: ("7045" or "4697")

attributes.title: 9. RAREST files created

attributes.description: Network (type 3) and RDP (type 10) logons. The same account fanning out from one source to many hosts is lateral movement.

query.query: winlog.logon.type: ("Network" or "RemoteInteractive" or "NetworkCleartext" or "NewCredentials") and source.ip: *

attributes.title: 10. Remote logons - source > target > account

attributes.description: Interactive remote desktop sessions, rarest accounts first. Service accounts or brand-new accounts using RDP deserve a look.

query.query: winlog.logon.type: "RemoteInteractive"

attributes.title: 11. RDP logons - rarest accounts

attributes.description: NTLM in a Kerberos domain is how pass-the-hash and relaying look. Rare accounts and unexpected sources first.

query.query: winlog.event_data.AuthenticationPackageName: "NTLM" or hayabusa.details.AuthenticationPackageName: "NTLM" or hayabusa.extra.AuthenticationPackageName: "NTLM"

attributes.title: 12. NTLM logons - rarest accounts

attributes.description: Event 4625. Many accounts from one source is spraying; many failures for one account is guessing.

query.query: event.code: "4625"

attributes.title: 13. Failed logons - source > account

attributes.description: Event 4769, rarest services first. A user requesting tickets for many services, or with RC4 (0x17) encryption, is Kerberoasting.

query.query: event.code: "4769"

attributes.title: 14. Kerberos service tickets - rarest services

attributes.description: Kerberos tickets issued with RC4. Modern domains use AES; RC4 requests are the classic Kerberoasting signature.

query.query: event.code: "4769" and (winlog.event_data.TicketEncryptionType: "0x17" or hayabusa.details.TicketEncryptionType: "0x17" or hayabusa.extra.TicketEncryptionType: "0x17")

attributes.title: 15. RC4 (0x17) service tickets
